text.p: Italian debt markets ended mixed on Friday, with the futures market managing to tick into positive territory while the cash market losing ground.
But dealers said the market's tone remained positive despite the future's failure to push higher with the same aggression it has shown recently.

Traders said Italian debt instruments were following U.S. markets and would continue to do so without any fresh domestic news. The February 2007 Btp ended down 20 basis points at 103.26, with the yield at 6.37 percent.
The 10-year Btp spread over the 10-year Bund was 83 basis points, shy of its record 80 basis points.
LIFFE September futures were up 10 basis points at 137.99, consolidating after hitting its latest record at 138.44 earlier this week.
Next week,"we'll follow foreign markets and react to developments in the dollar/mark trend," a broker said.
The Treasury said it would auction 9.5 trillion lire ($5.3 billion) medium- to long-term paper next week, much less than the 13 trillion analysts had forecast earlier in the week.
